title: TimescaleDB & Time-Series Engineering
description: Process billions of IoT metrics and stock ticks using Hypertables, automatic chunk partitioning, and continuous aggregates.

data.text: **TimescaleDB** is an extension that transforms PostgreSQL into a high-performance time-series database. It abstracts complex table partitioning behind **Hypertables**, automatically splitting data into time chunks without user intervention.

data.title: Creating a Hypertable with Continuous Aggregation
data.content: Automates downsampling of raw sensor readings into hourly rollups.
data.code:
-- 1. Create standard table
CREATE TABLE sensor_readings (
    recorded_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    device_id INT NOT NULL,
    cpu_temp NUMERIC,
    battery_pct NUMERIC
);

-- 2. Convert into TimescaleDB Hypertable partitioned by 7-day chunks
SELECT create_hypertable('sensor_readings', 'recorded_at', chunk_time_interval => INTERVAL '7 days');

-- 3. Fast time-bucket aggregation
SELECT 
    time_bucket('1 hour', recorded_at) AS hour_bucket,
    device_id,
    AVG(cpu_temp) AS avg_temp
FROM sensor_readings
WHERE recorded_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'
GROUP BY hour_bucket, device_id
ORDER BY hour_bucket DESC;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: TimescaleDB provides automatic chunk partitioning via Hypertables.
Delivers 10x-100x faster time-series analytical queries than vanilla PostgreSQL.
`time_bucket()` simplifies grouping metrics into arbitrary intervals (15m, 1h, 1d).
